## Custom Requirements

- App name: **Pira**. A Jira-inspired work management Code App backed by Dataverse.
- UX should feel as close to Jira as possible (top bar, project sidebar, board columns, issue detail panel, keyboard-friendly) while carrying its own visual identity.
- Theme: **charcoal surfaces with a single electric cyan accent** (user choice, 2026-10-14). No gradients/glows; every icon, avatar and status uses cyan or neutral grey only (current user's avatar is cyan, others grey; high/highest priority cyan, others grey).
- Light/dark mode toggle, remembered in localStorage (`pira-theme`); dark is the default. Light mode darkens accent text to `#007a8f` for contrast on white; fills stay `#00e5ff`.
- Scrollbars themed to match (thin, rounded, transparent track).
- Coding rules: user instructions in `Pira/.copilot/instruction.md` (identical to repo `.github/instructions/david.instructions.md`) — vanilla JS, camelCase with type prefixes (`b`/`i`/`s`/`a`/`o`/`e`), function-first, arrow callbacks, `"` for HTML attributes / `'` for JS strings, try/catch with friendly messages, cache to avoid repeat API calls, themed modals instead of alert/prompt.
- Build in phases; start with Phase 1 only (projects, members, issues, comments, history, My Work, basic Kanban).

## 2026-10-14 — Phase 1 build (UI-first)

- Decisions: environment Platform-Tools; publisher `wyattdave` / prefix `wd`; build the full UI on real Dataverse tables now, behind one data-service module, and move key allocation/transition/access checks into a C# plug-in + Custom APIs once a .NET SDK is available.
- Schema (`dist/config/dataverse-tables.json`): 10 user-owned tables — Project, Project Sequence, Project Member, Board, Board Column, Issue, Issue Comment, Issue History, Label, Issue Label. Issue primary name = immutable issue key so lookups display keys. Status is a local choice with a fixed default workflow (any→any) in `app-config.js`; board columns map to status values. Reporter/author/changed-by = server-stamped `createdby` (no client-trusted reporter column). Labels normalised (Label + Issue Label) instead of a delimited field. Workflow/Transition tables deferred (Phase 3 configurable workflows).
- Data access: `codeapp.js` CRUD plus the SDK client directly for paging (`maxPageSize` + `skipToken`, `$count`) because `listItems` drops the skip token (Dataverse has no `$skip`). Lookup navigation names resolved at runtime from `getEntityMetadata` (same approach as the Petty Cash app). Record GUIDs generated client-side (`crypto.randomUUID`) so creates need no re-query. Formatted-value annotations supply lookup names without `$expand`. Lookups cleared with `"<nav>@odata.bind": null` (confirmed on Microsoft Learn).
- Interim key allocation: read-increment the project sequence row, skip numbers already used, retry on alternate-key duplicate; uniqueness guarantee = `wd_issuekey` alternate key (manual step). Transitions re-read the server status before validating. Board moves are optimistic with full rollback on failure.
- UI from mockup 1: Your work (4 tabs + project tiles), Projects (search, archived toggle, create with key suggestion), project Board (server-side filters, per-column paging + counts, WIP, drag-and-drop + keyboard card menu with status/reorder), Issues list, Overview, Settings (details/key lock/archive, members with user search/roles/last-lead guard, columns name/WIP/order), issue panel (inline edits, transitions, labels, parent, comments with edit, history), global search, shortcuts C / `/` / M / Esc, light/dark.
- Bugs found and fixed during browser verification: `.card.sel` collided with the `.sel` select style (squashed cards) → `.is-selected` + `flex-shrink:0`; comment composer text was wiped when the list finished loading → composer rendered once per tab and draft kept; mock `clone(undefined)` threw on void operations; status pills misaligned list rows; link-buttons underlined.
- Verification: `npm test` 24/24 (14 domain, 9 service-level incl. 3 concurrent creates → unique keys, transitions, key immutability, last-lead, permission denied; 1 mock/service export parity); `npm run check` 13 modules OK; Playwright against the mock at 1528px and 820px, dark + light: all routes, create/transition/comment/filter/drag/menu/settings/archive flows, failure rollback (`piraMock.failNext`), stakeholder read-only, unknown project, deep link — 0 console errors. ## 2026-10-15 — Server logic as Dataverse low-code plug-ins

- Decision (user request): implement the server-side rules as **automated low-code plug-ins** (Power Fx, Dataverse Accelerator) instead of a C# plug-in / Custom APIs. Researched on Microsoft Learn: automated plug-ins are **preview** ("not meant for production use"); instant plug-ins are discontinued and replaced by Functions. Plug-ins run as the calling user, only on Create/Update/Delete, 2-minute limit; pre-operation `Set(NewRecord.X, …)` edits the in-flight row, `OldRecord`/`NewRecord` are full rows on Update, `Error()` blocks the save, `Collect` writes other tables, `User().EntraObjectId` identifies the caller.
- Eight plug-ins (docs/lowcode-plugins.md): Issue before/after create (membership, server key allocation with lock-then-read on the sequence row, initial status, Created history), Issue before update (immutable key/project, archived read-only, membership, transition table, parent rules, Resolved On, status/field/archive history), Comment before create (membership, history), Project before create/update (key format/uniqueness, lead = creator, key locked once issues exist, leads only), Member before create/update (leads only, creator bootstrap, last-lead guard, Removed On). Errors carry `[CODE]` prefixes mapped by `parseServerError`.
- App: `SERVER_LOGIC = 'lowcode'` (default) vs `'client'` fallback in app-config. In lowcode mode the client no longer allocates keys, stamps Resolved On or writes created/field/transition/archive/comment history; label history stays client-side (separate table). If the plug-in is missing, create fails with SERVER_LOGIC_MISSING and the unnumbered row is archived. Alternate-key duplicate still triggers the client retry.
- Not verifiable here: formulas cannot be compiled locally (no Power Fx runtime / Accelerator access); display names were taken from the generated schemas. Choice/Yes-No/Text() fallbacks documented. Concurrency of server allocation must be tested in the environment; the `wd_issuekey` alternate key remains the guarantee.
- Still open: per-project read security (plug-ins don't run on reads) → owner teams/sharing later. Labels/boards/columns writes not plug-in checked.
- Tests: `npm test` 31/31 (+4 lowcode-mode service tests with a plug-in emulating fake, +1 domain test for `[CODE]` parsing); `npm run check` OK.

## 2026-10-15 — Low-code plug-ins: no User() → Created By / Modified By

- Bug (reported by user on plug-in 1): "'User' is a recognized but not supported function". `User()` is listed in the Power Fx reference for Dataverse functions but is rejected in automated low-code plug-ins; no other current-user function exists there.
- Fix: identity checks moved to **post-operation** plug-ins that read the system-stamped `Created By` / `Modified By` from a fresh `LookUp` of the saved row. Synchronous post-operation runs in the same transaction, so `Error()` rolls back the save and any pre-operation side effects (key number, history). Pre-operation plug-ins keep user-independent work (key allocation, transitions, immutability, Resolved On, history). Now 11 plug-ins (was 8): Issue pre/post create, Issue pre/post update, Comment post create, Project pre create, Project pre/post update, Member post create, Member pre/post update. Plug-in 1 no longer references the user.
- Consequence: post-operation can't distinguish a lead stepping down from self-promotion, so nobody may change their own membership (another lead must); this also guarantees a remaining lead. Mirrored in the app (data-service + mock `assertNotSelf`, own row read-only in Settings → Members). Project Lead column is no longer forced by the server (informational only).
- Rollback verification added to the checklist (blocked create must leave no row/history). Flows/integrations updating Pira rows must run as project members.
- Verification: `npm test` 31/31 (membership test rewritten for the self rule), `npm run check` OK, mock browser check of Settings → Members (own row disabled, others editable, 0 console errors).

## 2026-10-15 — Low-code plug-ins: Status display-name clash

- Bug (user, plug-in 1): `Set(NewRecord.Status, 'Status (Issues)'.'To Do')` flagged on `NewRecord.Status`. Cause: Issues has two columns with display name "Status" — our `wd_status` and the system `statecode`. Power Fx `DisplayNameUtility.MakeUnique` (microsoft/Power-Fx source) rewrites colliding display names to `'Display (logical)'`, so plain `Status` no longer refers to our column.
- Fix: all record references in plug-ins 1 and 3 now use the logical name `wd_status` (15 replacements); logical names always resolve. Choice values `'Status (Issues)'.…` unchanged (not flagged). Doc note added. Board Columns has the same clash but isn't used in plug-ins; app code uses logical names, so no app change.
- File changes: docs/lowcode-plugins.md: +2 / -2 (plus 15 in-line replacements); dist/config/decision-log.md: this entry.

## 2026-10-15 — Pre-Phase 2 fixes and Phase 2 (agile delivery)

- User requests before Phase 2: (1) search people from Entra with the Office 365 Users connector; (2) parent lookups instead of typing keys; (3) switch boards and put an issue on more than one board; (4) "modifying tasks not working (no save button)". User choices (asked up front): create the Dataverse schema now with CAP; default board shows every issue and extra boards show only issues added to them; staged edits with a Save / Discard bar.
- **Save button.** The panel saved each field on change/blur and the summary on Enter, with no visible Save, so edits looked lost. Now every field is an always-editable control that updates a draft; a bar shows "N unsaved changes · Discard · Save" (Ctrl+S) and one `updateIssue` call saves everything. Closing, switching issue or reloading with unsaved edits asks first (route guard + `beforeunload`). Status stays an immediate action. Could not reproduce a hosted save failure here; if saves still fail in Dataverse, the toast now shows the plug-in's message.
- **People search.** `searchUsers` calls Office 365 Users `SearchUserV2` (connector wrapper copied unchanged from codeapp-js into `dist/connectors/`, loaded lazily), drops disabled / malformed results, then resolves Entra object IDs to Dataverse `systemuser` rows in one batched query. People without a Dataverse user are shown but can't be added (`USER_NOT_PROVISIONED`); `addMember` also refuses them. If the connector fails, it falls back to the Dataverse search.
- **Parents.** Type-ahead lookup (`pickers.js`, accessible combobox) in the panel and the create modal; server-filtered to allowed parent types in the same project. Decision: hierarchy is Epic (1) → Story (2) → Task/Bug (3) and a parent must be on a lower level. Strict levels make any new cycle impossible and are cheap to check in Power Fx (no recursion). The client still walks the ancestor chain to catch Phase 1 links that break the levels. Type changes are checked against the parent and children.
- **Boards.** Route `#/projects/KEY/board/<boardId>` (blank = default). New `wd_boardissue` junction; extra boards filter with `wd_issue_boardissue/any(...)` server-side. Board switcher, create/edit/archive boards (leads), per-board columns, Boards field in the panel, card menu add/remove. Board type Scrum shows only that board's active sprint.
- **Ranking.** Decision: one global rank per project, shared by backlog, sprints and boards (Jira's model), replacing per-status ranks. New issues go to the bottom. Every move sends neighbour **IDs**; the service re-reads their ranks and, if they're no longer in order (someone else moved them), ranks just after the issue above using its real successor. Equal ranks from simultaneous drops tie-break on created date then id, so every client sorts the same.
- **Sprints.** `wd_sprint` with Planned → Active/Cancelled, Active → Completed, Completed → Active (lead-only correction with a note). One active sprint per board (client + plug-in 13). Start requires dates and snapshots committed issues/points. Complete requires an explicit destination (backlog or an open sprint) when open issues exist, moves them first, then snapshots completed/incomplete counts and points. Not one transaction: a retry finishes a partial completion. Completed/cancelled sprints lock membership. Cancel (planned only) returns non-archived issues to the backlog.
- **Metrics.** Simple counts and sums, labelled "not a burndown": committed (start snapshot), completed, incomplete, scope change = net vs committed. Archived issues never count; unestimated = 0 points and listed. Dashboard counts use Dataverse `$count`, so they respect the caller's read access.
- **Story points** whole numbers 0–1000 (decision: no decimals); nullable. **Links** stored once From → To; inward choices swap the ends; no self links, no duplicate directed links, no contradictory pairs (A blocks B + B blocks A); Relates To is symmetric. Link history is written by the client in both modes (own table, like labels).
- **Dataverse.** CAP `createDataverseTable` in a disposable temp folder (repo untouched), order Sprint → Issue (adds Story Points + Sprint, existing table reused) → Board Issue → Issue Link; Board Issue and Issue Link needed the known 60 s retry. `capDataverse` registration in the same temp folder; schemas copied to `dist/config`, data sources and the Office 365 Users connection reference merged into `power.config.json` (and its `dist/config` copy).
- **Plug-ins.** Plug-ins 1 and 3 extended (type levels, sprint rules, sprint + story-point history); new 12–17 (Sprint before create/update, Sprint after create/update, Board Issue after create, Issue Link after create). Formulas can't be compiled here; display names come from the generated schemas.
- Bug found during review: cancelling a sprint tried to move archived issues, which plug-in 3 rejects (archived = read-only); archived issues are now left in place.
- Verification: `npm test` 53/53 (+10 domain, +12 service with an OData-evaluating Dataverse fake: placement with stale neighbours, simultaneous drops, one active sprint per board, completion destinations, locked sprints, lead-only reopen, cancel, parent cycles/types, links, Entra search + fallback, boards); `npm run check` 18 modules OK; mock browser run of backlog planning (menu + Alt+arrows), sprint complete (destination required), staged save + discard guard, parent lookup, child progress, links, board switch / remove from board, scrum board banner, settings boards + Entra search, overview, sprint reports — 0 console errors. The integrated browser runs hidden, so screenshots don't refresh and timers are throttled; checks were DOM-based. Snyk Code scan not run: CLI token expired (SNYK-0003).

## 2026-10-16 — Phase 3 (team productivity)

- User choices (asked up front, all the recommended options): create the Dataverse schema now with CAP; a fixed status catalogue (the four existing + Backlog, Blocked, In Testing, Closed) from which each project picks its list, order, initial status, transitions and required fields; in-app notifications plus a documented optional Power Automate outbox flow; attachments in a Dataverse file column; built-in templates (Kanban, Scrum, Bug tracking) at project creation and re-applicable from settings.
- **Workflows.** Stored per project: `wd_workflowstatuses` (ordered list), `wd_initialstatus`, `wd_workflowtemplate`, plus one `wd_workflowtransition` row per allowed move with `wd_require*` flags (resolution, assignee, story points, due date). Blank list = the Phase 1/2 default (any move), so existing projects are unchanged. Status categories (todo / progress / done) drive "done" logic, the open-only filter and metrics, so Closed counts as done. Removing a status in use is refused (`STATUS_IN_USE`). Transitions are deactivated, never deleted, so plug-ins and history stay consistent. Saving writes transitions first, then the project, then aligns every board's columns to the workflow; not one transaction, saving again completes it.
- **Server-side authority.** Plug-in 3 now reads the project's transitions and required fields; plug-in 1 uses the project's initial status; plug-in 7 checks board columns against the workflow. The app validates first for fast feedback, but the plug-ins are the authority (API writes are rejected the same way).
- **Resolution.** New Issue choice (Done, Won't Do, Duplicate, Cannot Reproduce); only valid on done-category statuses and cleared when an issue leaves them. Required only when a transition asks for it.
- **Saved filters.** Criteria stored as sanitised JSON; project is forced on load, "me" resolves to whoever runs it, so a shared filter never carries the owner's results or access. Owner-only edit/delete (User-level Write/Delete); plug-ins 30–31 require project membership and lock the project.
- **Bulk edit.** Up to 50 selected issues; preview first (per-issue "will change / already set / can't change" using the same workflow and permission checks), then one write per issue with per-issue results and retry of failures only. Decision: not atomic — Dataverse `$batch` change sets would roll back good rows on one bad one, which hides which issue failed. One summary notification per recipient.
- **Notifications.** `wd_notification` rows written best-effort after the save succeeds (failures logged, never rolled back or surfaced as save errors). No summaries/descriptions/comments stored, only key, event and a short phrase. Recipients must be active project members and never the actor; one notification per person per change (mention > assignment > status > comment). Mentions match the longest member names first. Bell polls every 2 minutes and on tab focus. Preferences per user (in-app event switches + email/Teams opt-in for the optional flow). The table doubles as the outbox (`wd_deliverystate`).
- **Attachments.** `wd_issueattachment` with a 10 MB file column; metadata row first, then the file, row deleted if the upload fails. Blocked executable/script extensions, sanitised names, 20 per issue. Download via the SDK into a Blob with `application/octet-stream` (never rendered inline). No public/anonymous links. Uploader-only delete.
- **Custom fields.** Five types (text, number, date, yes/no, single choice), per project, optionally per issue type; values in `wd_customfieldvalue` (one typed column per type, alternate key Issue + Field). Type can't change after creation; options removed from a choice field remain on existing issues as "(retired)". Values validated client-side and by plug-ins 22–23 (`INVALID_CUSTOM_FIELD_VALUE`). History field `cf:<name>`.
- **Dataverse.** CAP `createDataverseTable` in a disposable temp folder for the seven tables and new Project/Issue columns (some needed the 60 s MetadataCache retry). The CAP API skips existing columns, so the four new Status values were added to `wd_issue.wd_status` and `wd_boardcolumn.wd_status` with the `InsertOptionValue` Web API action + `PublishXml`; Board Column needed a short wait before publish. Registered with `capDataverse`; schemas copied to `dist/config`, data sources merged into both `power.config.json` files.
- Bugs found during review: `@Sam Ortiz` also notified a member called "Sam" (mentions now consume the longest match); `formatFileSize` reported MB wrongly; "1 issues still use" grammar.

## 2026-10-21 — Phase 4 (advanced capabilities)

- User choices (asked up front): build time tracking, releases and versions, advanced query builder, analytics, CSV import/export and dependency visualisation; **not** automation rules. Create the schema and deploy plug-ins to Platform-Tools. Design note per candidate in [docs/phase-4-design.md](../../docs/phase-4-design.md).
- **Feature flags.** `FEATURES` in `app-config.js` (all on). Off = UI hidden, sidebar links removed, routes "Page not found", and the data service throws `FEATURE_DISABLED` before any Dataverse call. Core CRUD untouched (tested with every flag off).
- **Time tracking.** Minutes everywhere; Jira-style durations (1d = 8h, 1w = 5d), bare numbers refused. Work logs never deleted: author edits/voids own, lead may only void others', voided logs locked; reason required. Remaining estimate auto-adjusts (never below 0) with a manual override (a second write; failure reported, log kept). *Time Spent* derived only by plug-ins 34–35; plug-in 1 blanks it on create and plug-in 36 replaces any direct change with the sum of the logs.
- **Releases.** One fix version per issue (lookup), not a many-to-many. Leads only (plug-ins 32–33). Fix version must be an unarchived version of the same project (plug-ins 1, 36). Release = move/clear/keep unfinished issues, then mark released; not one transaction, releasing again finishes it.
- **Advanced query.** Not JQL. Visual builder, AND/OR with one nested level, 20 rules, 30 values. Allowlist of fields/operators per kind in `app-config.js`; saved JSON sanitised on load, validated on run, translated by `buildQueryFilter` (strings escaped, GUIDs/numbers only after validation). Bug found: GUID values were quoted (Dataverse rejects them); fixed. Generated forms (`not any()`, `contains()` inside lambdas, nav names) verified with read-only `$top=1` queries against Platform-Tools.
- **Analytics.** Pure functions with documented definitions (lead/cycle time medians + 85th percentile nearest-rank, Monday weeks in local time, overdue trend from current values, sprint say/do from snapshots, estimate accuracy). *Started On* stamped once on first in-progress status (plug-ins 1, 36; client mode in the app). Reads capped at 2,000 issues per query with a notice. Power BI guidance: connect as each viewer, never a shared refresh account. Bug found: lead time wasn't limited to the window; `buildAnalytics` now windows itself.
- **CSV.** Export = current filter, ≤5,000, UTF-8 BOM, formula-injection guard. Import = parse → map headers → dry-run plan (same validation as create) → one create per row in file order → per-row results → retry failed rows only. ≤200 rows, ≤1 MB; status never imported. Bug found: CSV row errors used the uppercase field code; now short labels with hints.
- **Dependencies.** "Blocks" links laid out by Kahn levels; cycles flagged in a final column; external nodes dashed; "relates to" optional and never affects layout; text list for screen readers. ≤150 issues + 50 external.
- **Dataverse.** CAP `createDataverseTable` for Version, Work Log and the Issue columns; registered with `capDataverse`; schemas copied. dv-native: plug-in 1 replaced, 32–36 created, steps enabled with a Web API PATCH (imports arrive disabled). PS 5.1 splits unquoted comma lists for `--tables`. Plug-in 36 redeployed to protect Time Spent after the documentation review found direct writes weren't blocked.

Plug-ins compiled on import but not yet exercised with writes in Dataverse. Snyk Code scan not run (token still expired).

## 2026-10-21 — Phase 5 (Power Platform integration)

- Request: [phase-5-powerplatform-integration](../../phase-5-powerplatform-integration). The user wasn't available for questions, so the recommended options were taken: create the schema now with CAP, deploy plug-ins with dv-native, any lead/contributor (not stakeholders) may link solutions, and the story's chosen stage is UI-only (remembered in localStorage `pira-solution-stage`).
- **Connectors.** Generated with CAP in a disposable temp folder from *connected* connections (CAP's `capConnector` picks the first connection, which was in Error for Admins V2, so the runner chose the first Connected one). The previously copied template `powerplatformadminv2.js` was replaced by the generated one (its `ListEnvironmentsForUser` has no `ids` parameter). `commondataserviceforapps.js` is new. Both connection references merged into both `power.config.json` files.
- **Environments.** *Retrieve a list of environments* = `ListEnvironmentsForUser`, api-version `2024-10-01` (Microsoft Learn). Verified read-only against the Power Platform API: response `{ value: [{ id, displayName, type, url, state }] }`, `$top`/`$skip` honoured, URL without trailing slash. Only rows with a safe https Dataverse URL are kept; paging stops on a short page or a page with no new ids. Cached for the session TTL; client-side search.
- **Solutions.** Dataverse connector `ListRecordsWithOrganization(organization = env URL, 'solutions')` with `isvisible eq true` + `contains()` on friendly/unique name, first 50 by name; lookups by `solutionid` or `uniquename` (SchemaName). Filters built in `domain.js` (escaped, GUID/name validated before any call). Query shape verified read-only on Platform-Tools.
- **Data model.** `wd_epicsolution`: one row per epic and stage (Dev/Test/Stage/Prod choice), environment id/name/URL, solution id/unique name/name, plus a version + modified-on **snapshot** from when it was linked. Decision: unlinking empties the row instead of deleting it, so plug-in 38 checks every change and the role needs no Delete. Live versions are always re-read; the snapshot is shown only when the environment can't be read. `wd_issue.wd_solutionversion` (text 50) for stories.
- **Linking.** The service re-checks that the environment is in the user's own list and re-reads the solution by id from that environment before writing, so the browser can't plant versions, names or other hosts. Auto-select uses the SchemaName of the nearest linked stage (earlier stages first). Maker link `make.powerapps.com/environments/{envId}/solutions/{solutionId}` is built only from validated ids and opens with `noopener noreferrer`.
- **Story check.** Compares the **saved** solution version with the parent epic's live solution for the chosen stage: match / stage behind / stage ahead / no epic / no solution for the stage / solution deleted / environment unreadable. Versions compare numerically per segment, missing segments = 0. A story that changes type loses its version (client and plug-in 39).
- **Plug-ins.** 37 (Epic Solution after create), 38 (after update), 39 (Issue before update, Phase 5). Deployed into Pira-plugins; every import compiled (including `IsMatch`), steps enabled. dv-native's `Set()` warning on 39 is the known false positive. Not exercised with real writes yet (manual P1–P7). Plug-in 39 runs on every issue update; rollback = turn its step off.
- Bugs found in browser checks: the auto-select note named the first stage with that SchemaName instead of the stage actually used (now `pickAutoSelectSource`); dates older than a week showed the date twice.
- Verification: `npm test` 142/142 (+11 domain, +14 service with faked connectors and the OData-evaluating Dataverse fake: environment filtering/paging/caching/errors, solution filter escaping and unsafe hosts, link create/update/refusals, lowcode history, unlink without delete, story version rules, every check state, cache refresh; feature-flag test extended to Phase 5); `npm run check` 30 modules OK; mock browser run of epic link (auto-select, no-match note, required solution), live-version failure fallback, unlink + history, story stage tabs, invalid version blocked, save → check updates — 0 console errors. Snyk Code scan not run (SNYK-0003; needs `snyk auth`).

## 2026-10-21 — Fix: pickers clipped inside dialogs

- Bug (user): the environment list in "Link solution" opened inside the dialog's scrolling body and was clipped. Same for the solution list. Cause: `.combo-list` is absolutely positioned inside `.modal-body` (`overflow:auto`).
- Fix: inside a dialog, `wireCombobox` moves the list onto the scrim and positions it fixed under the input (above when space below is short), re-placing on body scroll/resize; the scrim host avoids the dialog's pop-in transform scaling it. Applies to every combobox in a dialog. The `*` now stays on the label line.
- Verification: mock browser: both lists sit 4px under their inputs, full width, topmost at their edges; selection still works. `npm test` 142/142, `npm run check` OK.
